summary: Round 3, test review. All four round-2 findings independently re-measured DEAD, each killed by exactly the test written for it and by no other: (1) deleting adopt's `held = null; heldVersion = null;` (LeaseManager.java:206-207, the LOSING branch of adopt, NOT renew's) fails only aLostAcquisitionDropsAnyBeliefFromAnEarlierTerm; (2) deleting the whole `ttl.isZero() || ttl.isNegative()` guard fails aNonPositiveTtlIsRefused AND aNegativeTtlOrRenewIntervalIsRefused, so the 'ttl must be positive' full-message assertion closed the equivalent-mutant hole; (3) `current.takenOverBy(podId, "", ...)` at the TAKEOVER call site fails only theEndpointIsAlsoWrittenOnTheTAKEOVERPathNotJustTheColdStart; (4) an unconditional `store.put` of an expired epoch-0 lease in renew's held==null branch fails only aNonHolderRenewIssuesNoRequestAtAll. The three round-1 majors were also re-measured after the file split and are all still dead (putIfAbsent->put kills whenTwoNodesBothSeeAnAbsentLease... and aLostAcquisition...; dropping `heldVersion = won.get()` kills aHolderCanRenewRepeatedly...; takeover adopting the CASed-from version kills aNodeThatTookOverCanThenRenew), plus release's putIfMatch->put kills aFencedHolderCannotReleaseSomeoneElsesLease. So the split preserved kill power. Suite measured at 483 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors; LeaseManagerTest at 29; check-tdd green ('29 new test(s), all observed failing first, unchanged since'); check-test-integrity green. Tree restored and re-hashed to a62849c5 after every mutation. StatBlindStore is sound: only `stat` is overridden, every mutating call delegates to the real MemoryBinStore, so the win/lose decision in both tests using it is made by a real conditional write, and the state it fabricates (two contenders both observing an absent key on a fresh prefix, or a stale HEAD between stat and the conditional write) is one production genuinely reaches. It does not license a pass production could not produce. Backlog row is now honest: it no longer claims all four round-1 minors were dead, it records that round 2 measured that claim FALSE for two of the four, and its claim that all four mutations are now dead individually is one I verified myself. Four minors below, none blocking; two are the round-2 minors deliberately left, and leaving them is correct per review.md rule 11.

findings.title: The cost test still names an acquire count it never asserts (carried from round 2, correctly not fixed)
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED. `acquiringCostsOneReadAndOneWriteAndRenewingCostsOneWrite` captures `afterAcquire` at line 278 and never asserts it; only the renew delta is constrained. Inserting a redundant `store.stat(key);` immediately before line 130's `Optional<ObjectStat> stat = store.stat(key);` in tryAcquire SURVIVES all 29 tests. theFirstAcquisitionUsesPutIfAbsent... does not catch it either, because it asserts `puts()` rather than `total()`. Production consequence is bounded -- an extra request per acquire is per-failover, not per-record, so cost.md's scaling rule is not at risk -- which is why this stays minor. Leaving it is right per rule 11: the fix is one assertion, but the round it would buy costs more than the hole. If it is written down, the honest form is that the test name over-promises, not that acquire is unpinned.

findings.title: `synchronized` on all four public methods is removable with the suite green -- belongs in a backlog row against M4.12, not a commit-body line
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED. Replacing all four occurrences of `public synchronized ` with `public ` leaves all 29 tests green, because every test drives one manager from one thread. The read-decide-CAS cycle interleaving with itself is the whole stated reason the keyword is there, and nothing in this suite can observe it. This is NOT a test defect this commit can repair: a T1 test with a MemoryBinStore cannot make a JVM interleave deterministically, and testing.md rule 20 already assigns exactly this class of property to the deterministic simulation. So it should become a BACKLOG ROW against M4.12 rather than a commit-body line -- a commit-body line dies with the commit and nothing will ever schedule it, whereas M4.12's simulation is the one place with the injectable interleaving that could kill the mutation. Recording it as prose here would be the weakest rung on non-negotiable 9's ladder.

findings.title: NEW: `renewInterval()` can return a hardcoded constant with the suite green -- the one accessor whose entire point is that it is NOT a constant
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED. Replacing `return renewInterval;` with `return Duration.ofSeconds(7);` SURVIVES all 29 tests. Only theRenewIntervalIsConfigurationNotAConstant reads the accessor and it constructs with exactly 7s, so the test cannot distinguish 'returns the configured value' from 'returns 7 seconds'. That is the precise defect the test is named for -- the backlog row's claim is 'TTL and renew interval are CONSTRUCTOR PARAMETERS, not constants', and M8's measurement loop is the caller that will read it. The kill is one more assertion at a second value (or asserting against the TTL/RENEW constants the class already has). Minor, not major, because the mutation is a hardcoded-literal one rather than a plausible edit, and because M8 changing the value would fail loudly at the call site. Do not fix in a fourth round -- record it.

findings.title: NEW: the key can ignore the `prefix` entirely with the suite green
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED. Replacing `String.format(Locale.ROOT, "%s/ctl/lease/%d.json", prefix, 0)` with `String.format(Locale.ROOT, "bins/cluster-a/ctl/lease/%d.json", 0)` SURVIVES all 29 tests. Every test that reaches the store uses prefix "bins/cluster-a"; the five tests that pass "p" all throw in the constructor and never touch the key. Production consequence if it were real: two clusters configured with different prefixes contend for one lease object, i.e. a cross-tenant leadership collision. Held at minor for two reasons -- the surviving mutant is the implausible hardcoded-literal kind, and the plausible variants die (substituting `podId` for `prefix` fails the assertion). Killed by one extra assertion on a manager built with a second prefix.

notes: Redundancy, informational, no action: aFencedHolderCannotRenewAndLearnsItFromTheEmptyResult (line 144) is strictly subsumed by aFencedHolderStopsBelievingItHoldsTheLease (line 353) -- identical setup, and the latter's assertions are a superset. exactlyOneOfTwoContendersAcquiresAnUnheldLease (line 94) is likewise subsumed by aHeldUnexpiredLeaseIsNotStolen (line 104), which asserts the same thing at the tighter TTL-1ms boundary. Neither is a defect and neither should be deleted -- both read as the behaviour they name, and volume is not the metric.

StatBlindStore route, informational: in aLostAcquisitionDropsAnyBeliefFromAnEarlierTerm the losing contender is the same instance that already won, which one production instance would not do. The BRANCH it exercises (adopt's losing path with `held` non-null) is nonetheless production-reachable via a lost takeover CAS, so the test constrains a real branch by an artificial route. No action.
